lines.trans: If I offended you, I ask your forgiveness.
No, now I must be by your side.
Together you and I will overcome everything.
Wait, what exactly will we overcome?
Katenka, Maxim told me everything.
And about your psychiatric condition too.
That you were treated in France, and it is secret.
I understand, wait for me for one minute.
Oh, how quickly time flies today!
It is already time for me and Victor to leave.
We do not eat after six at all.
We do not want to be fat.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'if', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Если не получится, я не виноват.
examples.trans: If it does not work out, it is not my fault.

examples.text: Если бы хотел, сразу бы нашёл.
examples.trans: If I wanted one, I would find one right away.

examples.text: Подумала, если тебя приглашу, он отстанет.
examples.trans: I thought if I invited you in front of him, he would back off.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Идеальное начало дня — бодрящий душ.
examples.trans: The ideal start to the day is an invigorating shower.

examples.text: Плотный завтрак и чашечка горячего кофе.

examples.text: Ой, Лёва, это очень горячо!
examples.trans: Ouch, Lyova, that is very hot!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты опять за Катей подглядывал?
examples.trans: Were you peeking at Katya again?

examples.text: Ладно, чего ты себя хоронишь?
examples.trans: Come on, why are you writing yourself off?

examples.text: Ты должен мне помочь с Катей.
examples.trans: You have to help me with Katya.

meanings.en: to offend, to hurt someone's feelings
meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'идеть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'offended, hurt', paired with 'обижать'.

examples.text: Если я тебя обидела, прошу прощения.
examples.trans: If I offended you, I ask your forgiveness.

examples.text: Извини, я не хотела обидеть.
examples.trans: Sorry, I didn't mean to offend you.

examples.text: Он никого не хотел обидеть.
examples.trans: He didn't want to offend anyone.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'сить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'ask for', paired with 'попросить'.

examples.text: Я хотел спросить у тебя совет.
examples.trans: I wanted to ask you for some advice.

examples.text: Слушай, я совсем забыл про это спросить.
examples.trans: Listen, I completely forgot to ask about that.

examples.text: Я прошу прощения.
examples.trans: I apologise.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'щение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'forgiveness' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Если я тебя обидела, прошу прощения.
examples.trans: If I offended you, I ask your forgiveness.

examples.text: Я прошу прощения.
examples.trans: I apologise.

examples.text: Он просит у меня прощения.
examples.trans: He is asking me to forgive him.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'no', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я понимаю, у меня нет шансов.
examples.trans: I understand, I do not have a chance.

examples.text: Мы вроде встречаемся, а вроде нет.
examples.trans: We are sort of dating, and sort of not.

examples.text: Подумала, если тебя приглашу, он отстанет.
examples.trans: I thought if I invited you in front of him, he would back off.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'now', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я вообще ничего теперь не понимаю.
examples.trans: I do not understand anything at all now.

examples.text: Нет, теперь я должен быть рядом.
examples.trans: No, now I must be by your side.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник.
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'лжен'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('must').

examples.text: Ты должен мне помочь с Катей.
examples.trans: You have to help me with Katya.

examples.text: К вечеру он должен найти женщину.
examples.trans: By tonight he has to find a woman.

examples.text: Или в гостиницу, продолжение банкета будет?
examples.trans: Or to a hotel, will there be a continuation of the party?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'be'.

examples.text: Нет, теперь я должен быть рядом.
examples.trans: No, now I must be by your side.

examples.text: Мы не хотим быть жирными.
examples.trans: We do not want to be fat.

examples.text: У меня есть машинка.
examples.trans: I have a toy car.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'beside', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Нет, теперь я должен быть рядом.
examples.trans: No, now I must be by your side.

examples.text: Лёва, у тебя с головой всё в порядке?
examples.trans: Lyova, is everything alright with your head?

examples.text: Место рядом с Григорием Сопрыкиным.
examples.trans: A plot next to Grigory Soprykin.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'together', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Если мы начнём жить с тобой вместе.
examples.trans: If you and I start living together.

examples.text: Вместе мы с тобой всё преодолеем.
examples.trans: Together you and I will overcome everything.

examples.text: Мы вместе.
examples.trans: We're together.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы вроде встречаемся, а вроде нет.
examples.trans: We are sort of dating, and sort of not.

examples.text: Мы ведь не спали до сих пор.
examples.trans: After all, we still have not slept together.

examples.text: Да, вот мы и договорились.
examples.trans: Yes, then it is settled between us.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with / from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Прости меня, пожалуйста, я случайно.
examples.trans: Forgive me, please, I did it by accident.

examples.text: Я понимаю, у меня нет шансов.
examples.trans: I understand, I do not have a chance.

examples.text: Ладно, чего ты себя хоронишь?
examples.trans: Come on, why are you writing yourself off?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Не всё, что говорят, чистая правда.
examples.trans: Not everything people say is the pure truth.

examples.text: Ты будешь во всём меня слушаться.
examples.trans: You will obey me in everything.

examples.text: Может, ещё не всё потеряно?
examples.trans: Maybe not everything is lost yet?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'we will overcome'.

related.gloss: not to we will overcome (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Вместе мы с тобой всё преодолеем.
examples.trans: Together you and I will overcome everything.

examples.text: Подожди, что именно мы преодолеем?
examples.trans: Wait, what exactly will we overcome?

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'wait', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, я сейчас.
examples.trans: Wait, I'll be right there.

examples.text: Подождите минуту.
examples.trans: Wait a minute.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А что, это так заметно, да?
examples.trans: Wait, is it really that noticeable?

examples.text: Не всё, что говорят, чистая правда.
examples.trans: Not everything people say is the pure truth.

examples.text: Я вообще не понимаю, что делать.
examples.trans: I do not understand what to do at all.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'specifically', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А на встречу идёшь именно ты.
examples.trans: And you are the one who goes to the meeting.

examples.text: Подожди, что именно ты знаешь?
examples.trans: Wait, what exactly do you know?

examples.text: Подожди, что именно мы преодолеем?
examples.trans: Wait, what exactly will we overcome?

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'сказать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'told', paired with 'рассказывать'.

examples.text: Катенька, мне Максим всё рассказал.
examples.trans: Katenka, Maxim told me everything.

examples.text: Расскажи, что случилось.
examples.trans: Tell me what happened.

examples.text: Я всё расскажу маме.
examples.trans: I'll tell Mum everything.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Идеальное начало дня — бодрящий душ.
examples.trans: The ideal start to the day is an invigorating shower.

examples.text: Плотный завтрак и чашечка горячего кофе.
examples.trans: A hearty breakfast and a little cup of hot coffee.

examples.text: Прости меня, пожалуйста, я случайно.
examples.trans: Forgive me, please, I did it by accident.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'about', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Прости меня, пожалуйста, я случайно.
examples.trans: Forgive me, please, I did it by accident.

examples.text: Ладно, я попробую устроить вам свидание.
examples.trans: Alright, I will try to arrange a date for you two.

examples.text: Я хотел спросить у тебя совет.
examples.trans: I wanted to ask you for some advice.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У неё серьёзное психическое расстройство.
examples.trans: She has a serious psychiatric disorder.

examples.text: Давайте выпьем за наше знакомство!
examples.trans: Let us drink to our acquaintance!

examples.text: И про твоё психическое заболевание тоже.
examples.trans: And about your psychiatric condition too.

meanings.note: Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('psychiatric, mental').

examples.text: У неё серьёзное психическое расстройство.
examples.trans: She has a serious psychiatric disorder.

examples.text: И про твоё психическое заболевание тоже.
examples.trans: And about your psychiatric condition too.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'болевание'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'illness, condition' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: И про твоё психическое заболевание тоже.
examples.trans: And about your psychiatric condition too.

examples.text: Это редкое заболевание.
examples.trans: This is a rare condition.

examples.text: У него инфекционное заболевание.
examples.trans: He has an infectious disease.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'also', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: И про твоё психическое заболевание тоже.
examples.trans: And about your psychiatric condition too.

examples.text: Я тоже.
examples.trans: Me too.

examples.text: Он тоже здесь.
examples.trans: He's here too.

meanings.en: to undergo medical treatment, be treated
meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'was treated, received treatment', paired with 'вылечиться'.

examples.text: Это лечится медикаментозно.
examples.trans: This is treated with medication.

examples.text: Он лечится в больнице.
examples.trans: He is being treated in the hospital.

examples.text: Это заболевание лечится медикаментозно.
examples.trans: This condition is treated with medication.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Плотный завтрак и чашечка горячего кофе.

examples.text: Ой, Лёва, это очень горячо!
examples.trans: Ouch, Lyova, that is very hot!

examples.text: Ты опять за Катей подглядывал?
examples.trans: Were you peeking at Katya again?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ой, Лёва, это очень горячо!
examples.trans: Ouch, Lyova, that is very hot!

examples.text: А что, это так заметно, да?
examples.trans: Wait, is it really that noticeable?

examples.text: Для тебя это дело привычное.
examples.trans: For you this kind of thing is familiar.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'екретно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Что ты лечилась во Франции, это секретно.
examples.trans: That you were treated in France, and it is secret.

examples.text: Макс сказал это совершенно секретно и спокойно.
examples.trans: Max said this quite secret and calmly.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'understood', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.text: Ты меня сейчас хорошо понял?
examples.trans: Did you understand me clearly just now?

examples.text: Я поняла, подожди меня одну минутку.
examples.trans: I understand, wait for me for one minute.

examples.text: Я поняла, подожди меня минутку.
examples.trans: I understand, wait for me a minute.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: На работу буду приходить на час позже.
examples.trans: I will come to work an hour later.

examples.text: Хорошо, договорились, приходи на час позже.
examples.trans: Alright, it is a deal, come an hour later.

examples.text: Погоди, ты что, мне не веришь?
examples.trans: Wait, do you not believe me?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'a minute' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Светочка, я на минутку отойду, не скучайте.
examples.trans: Svetochka, I will step away for a minute, do not be bored.

examples.text: Я поняла, подожди меня одну минутку.
examples.trans: I understand, wait for me for one minute.

examples.text: Я поняла, подожди меня минутку.
examples.trans: I understand, wait for me a minute.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'oh', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ой, Лёва, это очень горячо!
examples.trans: Ouch, Lyova, that is very hot!

examples.text: А Дима сейчас в полной растерянности.
examples.trans: But Dima is in complete bewilderment right now.

examples.text: У нас с тобой разница шесть лет!
examples.trans: There is only a six-year difference between us!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А они вон какие разные люди.
examples.trans: And look how different those two people are.

examples.text: Посмотри, какой я молодой и поджарый.
examples.trans: Look how young and lean I am.

examples.text: На моей кухне никаких интрижек не потерплю!
examples.trans: I will not tolerate any flings in my kitchen!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Что случилось, Макс? Говори быстрее.
examples.trans: What happened, Max? Tell me quickly.

examples.text: Быстро пошли вон отсюда работать!
examples.trans: Get out of here quickly and go work!

examples.text: Тогда всё быстрее начнёт двигаться у нас.
examples.trans: Then everything will start moving faster for us.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.text: Сегодня же у меня будет женщина.
examples.trans: This very day I will have a woman.

examples.text: Ладно, тогда до сегодняшнего вечера.
examples.trans: Alright, until this evening then.

examples.text: Сегодня у меня будет женщина!
examples.trans: Today I will have a woman!

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'time' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Сколько же вам надо времени?
examples.trans: Just how much time do you need?

examples.text: Можешь двумя руками одновременно рисовать фигуры?
examples.trans: Can you draw shapes with both hands simultaneously?

examples.text: Ой, как быстро сегодня время летит!
examples.trans: Oh, how quickly time flies today!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is flying', paired with 'полететь'.

examples.text: Летим! Хоп!
examples.trans: We're flying! Hop!

examples.text: Завтра я лечу в Москву.
examples.trans: Tomorrow I'm flying to Moscow.

examples.text: Все видели, как ты из окна летел.
examples.trans: Everyone saw you fly out the window.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А ты уже старая развалюха.
examples.trans: And you are already an old wreck.

examples.text: Алло, да, Дима, вы уже в ресторане?
examples.trans: Hello, yes, Dima, are you in the restaurant already?

examples.text: Ведь я уже совсем не мальчик.
examples.trans: After all, I am not a boy anymore.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'it's time', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы ведь не спали до сих пор.
examples.trans: After all, we still have not slept together.

examples.text: Ты в паспорт мой не смотри.
examples.trans: Do not look at my passport.

examples.text: Давай поспорим с тобой на зарплату!
examples.trans: Let us bet a month's salary on it!

meanings.en: to go, to drive, to ride
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go', paired with 'поехать'.

examples.text: Зачем ехать ко мне домой?
examples.trans: Why would we go to my place?

examples.text: Нам уже пора ехать с Викторией.
examples.trans: It is already time for me and Victor to leave.

examples.text: Виталик, в Санта-Фе едем.
examples.trans: Vitalik, we're going to the Santa Fe.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще').

examples.text: Я вообще не понимаю, что делать.
examples.trans: I do not understand what to do at all.

examples.text: Старость ведь вообще никого не щадит.
examples.trans: Old age spares no one at all, after all.

examples.text: Лене вообще надо памятник ставить.
examples.trans: They should put up a monument to Lena.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я понимаю, у меня нет шансов.
examples.trans: I understand, I do not have a chance.

examples.text: Ты должен мне помочь с Катей.
examples.trans: You have to help me with Katya.

examples.text: Чего? Я не буду помогать.
examples.trans: What? I am not going to help.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to eat', paired with 'съесть'.

examples.text: У нас с тобой разница шесть лет!
examples.trans: There is only a six-year difference between us!

examples.text: Честно говоря, я сам не знаю почему.
examples.trans: Honestly, I do not know why myself.

examples.text: Добрый день, я шеф-повар этого ресторана.
examples.trans: Good afternoon, I am the head chef of this restaurant.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'after', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я серьёзно, ну сам посуди.
examples.trans: I am serious, just judge for yourself.

examples.text: Сочувствую, ведь это был последний шанс.
examples.trans: I sympathize, after all that was your last chance.

examples.text: Посмотри, какой я молодой и поджарый.
examples.trans: Look how young and lean I am.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'six', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У нас с тобой разница шесть лет!
examples.trans: There is only a six-year difference between us!

examples.text: Мы вообще не едим после шести.
examples.trans: We do not eat after six at all.

examples.text: Девять, шесть, шесть.
examples.trans: Nine, six, six.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.text: Я хотел спросить у тебя совет.
examples.trans: I wanted to ask you for some advice.

examples.text: Если бы хотел, сразу бы нашёл.
examples.trans: If I wanted one, I would find one right away.

examples.text: Привет, Макс, я хотела тебе сказать.
examples.trans: Hi, Max, I wanted to tell you something.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('fat').

examples.text: Мы не хотим быть жирными.
examples.trans: We do not want to be fat.

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень жирный выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very fat choice.
